subject: MidtownPay: post-demo model recommendations and follow-ups
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Jared Coleman <jared@midtownpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: MidtownPay demo follow-up — recommended models, benchmarks, next steps

Hi Jared — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) What we heard
- Primary use: automated dispute triage + suggested response snippets for customer service; median snippet length ~45–80 tokens.
- Key success criteria: precision on top-1 suggestion (must be >= 88%), latency P95 < 150ms, and reproducible behavior on legal/terms-sensitive prompts.

2) Model recommendations (based on your dataset profile and latency targets)
- rwd-llm-moderate-16k@v1.7-stable — best balance of cost and precision on our bench.
- rwd-llm-high-8k@v2.0-experimental — higher precision on edge cases, heavier cost; recommend for a follow-on A/B.

3) Artifacts I uploaded to the shared drive (links below)
- evaluation workbook with per-prompt metrics (midtown_benchmarks_v2.xlsx)
- curated prompt bank for your representative flows (prompt_set_v1.txt)
- small sample of anonymized production examples you can use to sanity-check outputs

4) Immediate asks / next steps
- Can your engineering team share the last two production request IDs where you saw the regression? Having the raw inputs helps our eval team triage quickly.
- We'd like permission to run a focused diff between v1.7-stable and v2.0-experimental against the provided prompt set. If you want safety, we can run this in your sandbox/with obfuscated tokens.
- If the issue is blocking production, we can propose a temporary pin to v1.7-stable while we complete the regression investigation — typical turnaround for a pin + rollout is 24–48 hours once legal/ops approve.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1MidtownPayBenchmarkPack
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/MP-2026-57

Attachments: midtown_benchmarks_v2.xlsx, prompt_set_v1.txt

Thanks — I’ve CC’d Marcus (our model ops lead) and Monica (your solutions engineer) who will own triage and the pin plan.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

On Mon, Nov 29, 2026 at 09:14 AM Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Jared — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned:

Thanks Aisha — appreciate the clear next steps. A couple of things from our side after a quick look at the benchmark pack: 

- We started seeing a subtle but material behavior change in production last week, right after an internal rollout of what we believe is model tag rwd-llm-moderate-16k@v1.8 (our infra team recorded the change on 2026-11-25 02:10 UTC). The surface issue: for ~6% of dispute categories the suggested snippet now omits required policy language (we include a short required sentence), which previously was consistently included.

- I attached two request/response pairs (diff_examples.json) showing the behavior. The change is enough that our compliance reviewers flagged it and paused a wider rollout.

Ask: can Redwood confirm whether v1.8 included any prompt-rewriting or safety-filter tightening that could explain this drift? If not, we’d like to request a pin back to v1.7-stable for our production traffic while you triage. We’re happy to do a short canary with 10% traffic if that helps.

Also — our legal team prefers any pinning to be documented as a Service Change Request so we can track the authorization.

—Jared
Jared Coleman
Head of Product, MidtownPay
platform@midtownpay.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jared Coleman <jared@midtownpay.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MidtownPay demo follow-up — recommended models, benchmarks, next steps

Thanks for the examples, Jared — and thanks for surfacing timestamps. We’ll treat this as a priority. Short plan below.

1) Quick triage (ETA: 6–12 hrs) - I’ll kick off a differential evaluation between v1.7-stable and the v1.8 snapshot you referenced using the prompt_set_v1.txt you approved. That will produce per-prompt token-level diffs and highlight any token suppression / safety-filter changes. Expect a short excerpt (diff_report_excerpt.txt) by EOD PST.

2) Interim mitigation (ETA: 24–48 hrs) - Proposed mitigation is to pin MidtownPay’s production route to rwd-llm-moderate-16k@v1.7-stable. Operational notes: pinning is a config change on our routing layer — no data migration required. We can implement a 10% canary within 4 hours of signoff and full pin within 24 hours of ops approval.

3) Compliance / legal documentation - We’ll generate a Service Change Request document (I’ve attached proposed_pin_change.docx) capturing scope, rollback criteria, and expected impact. Please have your legal sign-off cadence; we can accept DocuSign for approval.

4) Root-cause follow-up (ETA: 3 business days)
- If diffs point to model-side changes (e.g., safety-filter thresholds, tokenization tweaks), we’ll collaborate with our model team to propose remediation (retraining, prompt-template adjustments, or fixed post-processing for required clauses).

Attachments: diff_report_excerpt.txt (will follow), proposed_pin_change.docx

Jared — can you confirm the production request IDs or provide a short list of representative request_ids? Also confirm who on your legal/ops side should be on the Service Change Request.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Lead, Model Ops | Redwood Inference
